rules.heading: # JBIT
lines: JBIT (`/jbit:plan`, `/jbit:stage`, `/jbit:autopilot` and the other `/jbit:<name>` skills) runs a project from one plan file, `docs/PLAN.md`.

- **Read `CLAUDE.md` first.** A project using JBIT keeps its working rules in `CLAUDE.md` at the repo root, which this host doesn't load. At the start of a session, and before any JBIT skill, read that file if it exists and follow it as you would `AGENTS.md`. Where a skill reads or writes `CLAUDE.md`, use that file, not `AGENTS.md`; JBIT never writes the project's `AGENTS.md`.
- **Skills.** Type a skill as `/jbit:<name>` (for example `/jbit:plan`); that form expands it. When a skill says to run another JBIT skill, open that skill's `SKILL.md` and follow it.
- **Host names.** Each JBIT skill ends with an "On Antigravity CLI" section that maps the names its text and its hook's messages use to this host's tools. Read it before acting on a skill.

mapping.heading: ## On Antigravity CLI
lines: JBIT was written for Claude Code; this copy is generated for Google Antigravity CLI (`agy`). Where the text or the hook's messages use Claude's names, read them this way:
- **Instructions.** Antigravity loads `AGENTS.md` and `GEMINI.md`, not `CLAUDE.md`. Where a skill reads or writes `CLAUDE.md`, use that file, and read it yourself at the start of a session.

- **Skills.** A `jbit:<name>` skill is typed `/jbit:<name>` (for example `/jbit:plan`), which Antigravity expands into the prompt. When a skill says to run another JBIT skill, open that skill's `SKILL.md` (its path is in your skill listing) and follow it.

- **Agents.** An Agent call is `invoke_subagent`: give it the role and the brief as its prompt. Agents take no per-call model or effort, so a plan's Models line can't be applied here: the subagent runs on the session's model. JBIT's role agents don't ship on Antigravity: brief a plain `invoke_subagent` with the role. A subagent reports back with `send_message`.

- **No worktree isolation.** JBIT doesn't rely on `isolation: "worktree"` here. Build leaves one at a time in the main tree, or in parallel only when each builder owns files no other touches; there is no branch to merge back.
- **Questions.** Where a skill says to ask the user (AskUserQuestion on Claude Code), use `ask_question`, or ask in the chat and wait for the reply.
- **Reviews.** `/code-review` and `/security-review` are Claude Code commands. Here, run a fresh `invoke_subagent` briefed with the same lenses (correctness, then security), and triage what it finds.

- **Hooks.** JBIT's hook puts the plan's `## Now` into context once per prompt, gates commits, guards secrets and the host's config, holds edits and subagents while a stage is held, and carries autopilot on at a turn's end (at most 8 times per prompt). `/hooks` lists its six events.

- **Script paths.** `<this skill's folder>` and `<verify skill folder>` in a skill's command are placeholders: put in the folder holding that skill's `SKILL.md` in the installed JBIT plugin (its path is in your skill listing), never a path inside the project (a project's own `scripts/capture.mjs` isn't JBIT's). Run the script by that full path from the project, so its other paths (`--out docs/evidence/…`) stay relative to the project. Screenshots come only from that script; the host's browser tools aren't a fallback.
- **Tools.** {tools}. Edits go through `write_file` and `edit_file`; the guard covers them and the shell alike.

gaps.why: agy runs a tool call when its PreToolUse hook prints nothing (proven in the spike, hooks-deny/13, 14). The shipped hook prints an explicit allow or deny on every path, a crash, bad input, an unknown event and an old Node included, and its 25-second watchdog answers before agy's 30-second timeout.

gaps.what: A subagent's calls judged in its parent's session, when linked
gaps.why: agy's payload marks no subagent and names no parent: the hook reads the parent from agy's own first message in the subagent's transcript (or its message files) and judges the subagent's calls in the parent's session, as Claude Code does. When it can't link one, it judges the calls as armed, attended, with no stage approved, the strictest any session could be. A held stage still refuses `invoke_subagent` itself, so no subagent starts while a stage is held.

agy honours 10 Stop continues per prompt and never sets `continuationActive`, so the hook counts its own: at most 8 continues per user prompt, reset only by the user's next prompt (not by a subagent waking the session), kept in its data folder, which the guard keeps tools from writing.

gaps.what: `## Now` copies in a long conversation
gaps.why: agy keeps every injected step, so the plan's `## Now` is injected once per prompt (on its first model call) and the copies pile up one per prompt, and again on a resumed conversation.

Writes to `~/.gemini/config/`, `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` and the plugins' data folders are refused through write_file, edit_file and shell commands that name them, but the shell check is best-effort: a command that reaches them without naming them isn't caught. The rest of `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/` stays writable.
The guard compares paths case-sensitively, so on a case-insensitive file system a write to `.Gemini/config` can slip past it.

gaps.what: Writes through the shell in a held stage
gaps.why: The hold refuses write_file, edit_file and `invoke_subagent`, but a file written by a shell command isn't held, on any host.
The hook runs the Claude hook's TypeScript through Node's type stripping; an older Node can't load it, so guarded tool calls are refused.

gaps.what: Lean's count of agents already running
gaps.why: Each hook event is a fresh process, so no in-memory agent list carries between events.

gaps.what: The reopen check after a commit
gaps.why: It runs before the commit lands, since there's no in-memory state carried to the next event.

gaps.what: Compacting the context before autopilot carries on
gaps.why: agy gives a command hook no context gauge and no compact call.
agy expands a skill only as `/jbit:<name>`. A bare `/plan` reaches the model as plain text, which may still read the skill, as may a prompt that describes the task, with no guarantee.

gaps.what: A headless run without allow rules
gaps.why: In `--mode accept-edits` every shell command asks, and `agy -p` can't ask, so it denies any command no `permissions.allow` rule covers (exit 0, `denied_actions`) and the stage stops there; in live runs that was an ordinary `ls`, `echo` or `date`. Pass the README's narrow rules with `--settings`; a broad `command(git)` or `command(node)` lets `git push` and `node -e` run unprompted.
An agy agent takes `model` as `inherit`, `flash` or `pro`, with no effort, so the Models line's model half applies and its effort half doesn't.
A plugin can't set one in agy; it is a user setting, and its input carries the account's email, so a status line script should never log it whole.
agy loads `AGENTS.md` and `GEMINI.md`, not `CLAUDE.md`; the package's rules tell the model to read `CLAUDE.md` itself.
They need a running Chrome with remote debugging and a person clicking Allow, so screenshots come only from the capture script.
The hook allows a tool only when it is read-only or on its list, so a tool a newer agy adds is refused until JBIT lists it.
`notebook_execution` runs arbitrary code with no command line to judge, so the hook refuses it.

gaps.what: Commits and pushes from a script or alias
gaps.why: The gates read the command line, as on every host, so a commit or push run inside a script, an interpreter or an alias defined elsewhere isn't seen.
